newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE ENGLISH LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP. [CORRECTED 10:07 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE ENGLISH LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP. [CORRECTED 10:07 GMT]

text.p: The following matches are scheduled to take place this weekend in the English league championship:
(All matches kickoff 1400 gmt unless stated)
Saturday
Arsenal (2) v Coventry City (19)

Arsenal, still likely to be without Dennis Bergkamp, could go top if they win new manager Arsene Wenger's first home match in charge against an under-achieving Coventry who have scored just once away.
Aston Villa (8) v Leeds (15)

A week after his already infamous Nazi-style salute, goalkeeper Mark Bosnich makes his first home appearance of the season after injury. Leeds, eager to avenge the hammering Villa gave them in the League Cup final, will have captain Ian Rush, 35 on Sunday, back after hamstring trouble.
Chelsea (6) v Wimbledon (5)

High-flying Wimbledon make the short trip to Chelsea looking for their seventh successive league win -- and could even go top for 24 hours at least if they win. Chelsea Player-manager Ruud Gullit is recovering full fitness, but unlikely to play.
Middlesbrough (9) v Tottenham (11)
England international Nick Barmby faces his old team as Middlesbrough look to end a run of three league games without a win against an erratic Tottenham side who play better away than at home.
Nottingham Forest (17) v Derby County (14)

A Midlands derby between the two clubs who won the title under Brian Clough in the 1970s. Saturday's game is more about league survival than trophies with Forest looking for their first win since the first day of the season.
Sheffield Wednesday (7) v Blackburn Rovers (20)
Wednesday have nosedived since winning their first four games and they will be looking for their first win in five against Blackburn, the only team without any league wins at all.
Southampton (18) v Sunderland (13)

Manager Graeme Souness is likely to give home debuts to new signings Israeli Eyal Berkowicz and Norwegian Egil Ostendstad against a promoted Sunderland side holding their own under coach Peter Reid, captain of Everton in the 1980s (Corrects from 1970s) when his opposite number at Liverpool was...Souness.
West Ham (16) v Leicester City (12)
Promoted Leicester's last visit to London ended in a late 2-1 win at Tottenham and they could repeat that scoreline against a West Ham team whose multi-national team has so far failed to gel.
Sunday
Liverpool (3) v Everton (10)
The 155th Merseyside league derby sees Liverpool looking like championship contenders and Everton looking to consolidate a recent improvement in their form.
Newcastle United (1) v Manchester United (4) 1500 GMT

For the second time in a week, unbeaten Manchester United face the taple-toppers. They knocked Liverpool off the top last week while Newcastle, after their heart-break at the hands of United last season, will be desperate to win this one.
